_comment: Page-level copy for the field-guide redesign. Route-level copy lives in routes.json under each route's `almanac` key. Every string here is final: it is not rewritten for SEO, cut into bullets or translated.

home.editorNote: There are three routes here and I have walked two of them, end to end, and those two I would send anybody on. The third I have put together from places I know separately, which is not the same thing, and I would rather say so than pretend otherwise.
home.colophon: Written in London in March, and corrected whenever somebody tells me I am wrong.
home.unwalkedHead: One I have not walked yet, so there is no photograph of it.

index.eyebrow: The index · every route, walked or not
index.title: Everything, in the order I trust it.
index.intro: Walked routes first, then the ones I have put together. The five facts on every line are the same five you get on the route page, in the same order.
index.walkedHead: Walked, and I would send you.
index.unwalkedHead: Put together from places I know.
index.unwalkedNote: Order and timings are my guess. No photographs, because I have not stood there with this route in mind.
index.scale: Three words for effort, used the same way on every route: flat, gentle, a proper walk. They are defined in {termsLink}.

terms.title: Terms used here.
terms.intro: Five words do most of the work on this site. If any of them means something different to you, the routes will read wrong, so here is what I mean by each.

definitions.body: Pavement and level ground the whole way. You could do it in the shoes you happen to have on.
A few miles, one or two slopes, nothing that needs a plan. You will know you have walked, and that is all.
Hills, mud after rain, and a real reason to sit down at the end. Wear something you do not mind ruining.
I have done this route start to finish, in this order, and the timings are measured rather than estimated. Walked routes carry a photograph I took, dated in the caption.
I know the places, not the joins. The order is my judgement and the timing is a guess. There is no photograph, and the line where one would sit says why.
One person, travel not included. Next to nothing means under a tenner if you skip the pub. Under £30 assumes one drink and something to eat. Anything above that, I say so in the route.
Where I know there is one you can use without buying anything, and where you will have to buy a drink. Not exhaustive, and I would like to be corrected.

terms.legacyHead: Words this site uses on purpose.
terms.legacyNote: Not a style guide. Each of these is doing a specific job, and most of them are there to protect you from a bad day out.

legacy.body: Not the same as an old pub. An old pub can be ruined by one refit; an old room survives its owners. You know one when your voice drops slightly on entering.
A named station within a short walk of every stage, and — more importantly — permission. Leaving a route early is a version of the route, not a failure of it.
What the route page owes you: names, minutes, and what to do when the pub is full. Mood is the reason to go; the useful version is how.
Written before what to expect, and taken more seriously. Most bad days out are caused by accurate places and inaccurate hopes.
Walked, in person, recently enough to say so with a date. Nothing else on this site borrows that word, because assembling a route from knowledge is not the same as standing in it.
Walked once, in person, but not lately. The shape has been stood in; some live details — hours, prices, whether the place still exists — need checking before you go.
An honest draft. The shape is right; the details have not been stood next to. Treat every fact on a prototype as a rumour with good posture.
The last stop, chosen so that the day has an ending rather than a trailing-off. Usually an old room. Never a queue.
The feeling this site is for. Not another city — just enough sideways distance from your usual London that the evening acquires a border, and therefore a shape.

terms.closing: If a route uses a word that is not on this page, that is a mistake and worth telling me about.

corrections.lead: River first. Pub later. Routes with a beginning, a useful pause, and no obligation to make a big day of it.
corrections.body: If you go, tell me what was too loud, too long, unexpectedly good or not worth the trip. Corrections go into the next edition with your wording where I can keep it.
corrections.scale: Three words for effort, used the same way every time: flat, gentle, a proper walk. They are defined in {termsLink}.
